theme: Cornelius, the Gentiles receive the Spirit
readingInstruction: Read Acts 10:1-11:30. God sends Peter to the household of Cornelius, a Roman centurion, and the Holy Spirit falls on Gentiles. Peter defends this in Jerusalem, and the church at Antioch is born. This is the hinge of Acts.
settingTheScene: Cornelius, a centurion in Caesarea, is a God-fearer who prays and gives alms. Peter is in Joppa, hungry, praying on a rooftop. God arranges both visions to bring them together. For a Jew to enter a Gentile house was against custom, and it was a major step. The conversion of Cornelius opens the door for Gentiles to enter the church without becoming Jews first.
observation: “A devout man who feared God with all his household, gave alms generously to the people, and prayed continually to God” (10:2).
“What God has made clean, do not call common” (10:15).
“Truly I understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him” (10:34).
“To him all the prophets bear witness that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name” (10:43).
“While Peter was still saying these things, the Holy Spirit fell on all who heard the word” (10:44).
“Then to the Gentiles also God has granted repentance that leads to life” (11:18).
“When he came and saw the grace of God, he was glad, and he exhorted them all to remain faithful to the Lord with steadfast purpose” (11:23).
“And in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians” (11:26).
interpretation:
Peter has a vision of a sheet lowered from heaven filled with animals, clean and unclean. A voice says, “Rise, Peter; kill and eat.” Peter objects: “I have never eaten anything that is common or unclean.” The voice replies, “What God has made clean, do not call common.” This happens three times. While Peter wonders about the vision, the men from Cornelius arrive. The Spirit tells Peter to go with them. He realizes that the vision was not just about food but about people. “God has shown me that I should not call any person common or unclean.”

At Cornelius’s house, a crowd has gathered. Peter says, “Truly I understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.” He then preaches the gospel: Jesus of Nazareth, anointed with the Holy Spirit and with power, went about doing good, was killed by hanging on a tree, and raised on the third day. “To him all the prophets bear witness that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.” Notice: forgiveness is received through faith in him. While Peter is still speaking, the Holy Spirit falls on all who hear. The Jewish believers with Peter are amazed that the gift of the Holy Spirit has been poured out on Gentiles, for they hear them speaking in tongues and extolling God. Peter asks, “Can anyone withhold water for baptizing these people who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?” They are baptized.

When Peter returns to Jerusalem, believers criticize him: “You went to uncircumcised men and ate with them.” Peter explains step by step. “If then God gave the same gift to them as he gave to us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could stand in God’s way?” They fall silent and glorify God: “Then to the Gentiles also God has granted repentance that leads to life.”

Meanwhile, those scattered after Stephen’s death have reached Antioch, where some preached to Greeks as well, and many believed. The Jerusalem church sends Barnabas, who sees the grace of God and rejoices, then fetches Saul. For a year they teach a great company, “and in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians.” The church in Antioch will become the base for the first missionary journey.
connection: Leviticus 11 is the food laws. Genesis 12:3 promised blessing to all nations through Abraham. Isaiah 49:6 is the light to the Gentiles. Deuteronomy 10:17 says God is not partial. Ephesians 2:11-22 describes the Gentiles made near. Galatians 2:11-14 shows Peter struggling again with table fellowship. Romans 2:11 and 3:29-30 say God is the God of Gentiles as well. Mark 7:19 says Jesus declared all foods clean.
application:
Ask who you have been treating as “common or unclean,” and ask God to change your view.

Invite someone from a different background to share a meal with you this week.

Remember that you are among the Gentiles to whom God granted repentance that leads to life.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he shows no partiality.
Thank him for sending the gospel to you.
Ask him to forgive where you have shown partiality.
